studies.Reference: Plasma carotenoids, retinol and tocopherol levels and the risk of ovarian cancer.
studies.Authors: Jeong NH, Song ES, Lee JM, Lee KB, Kim MK, Cheon JE, Lee JK, Son SK, Lee JP, Kim JH, Hur SY, Kwon YI
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Preoperative plasma concentrations of retinol were measured by reverse-phase, gradient high-pressure liquid chromatography.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Forty-five epithelial ovarian cancers and 135 age-matched controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Women with the highest tertiles of retinol (OR 0.45; 95%CI 0.21-0.98) had lower risk of ovarian cancer than women in the lowest tertiles.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Women in the highest tertile for retinol had lower risk of ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.042.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We investigated the relation between plasma carotenoids, retinol and tocopherol levels and ovarian cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Preoperative plasma concentrations of retinol were measured.

studies.Reference: Risk of ovarian carcinoma and consumption of vitamins A, C, and E and specific carotenoids: a prospective analysis.
studies.Authors: Fairfield KM, Hankinson SE, Rosner BA, Hunter DJ, Colditz GA, Willett WC
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Women reported on known and suspected ovarian carcinoma risk factors including reproductive factors, smoking, and use of vitamin supplements on biennial mailed questionnaires from 1976 to 1996. Food frequency questionnaires were included in 1980, 1984, 1986, and 1990.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: among 80,326 participants in the Nurses' Health Study
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The multivariate relative risks (95% confidence intervals [CIs]) for ovarian carcinoma among women in the highest versus lowest quintile of intake were 1.04 (95% CI, 0.72-1.51) for vitamin A from foods and supplements
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: The authors observed no association between ovarian carcinoma risk and antioxidant vitamin consumption from foods, or foods and supplements together.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.836.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: The authors confirmed 301 incident cases of invasive epithelial ovarian carcinoma during 16 years of dietary follow-up (1980-1996).
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: The multivariate relative risks (95% confidence intervals [CIs]) for ovarian carcinoma among women in the highest versus lowest quintile of intake were 1.04 (95% CI, 0.72-1.51) for vitamin A from foods and supplements.

studies.Reference: Intake of vitamins A, C, and E and folate and the risk of ovarian cancer in a pooled analysis of 10 cohort studies.
studies.Authors: Koushik A, Wang M, Anderson KE, van den Brandt P, Clendenen TV, Eliassen AH, Freudenheim JL, Genkinger JM, Håkansson N, Marshall JR, McCullough ML, Miller AB, Robien K, Rohan TE, Schairer C, Schouten LJ, Tworoger SS, Wang Y, Wolk A, Zeleniuch-Jacquotte A, Smith-Warner SA
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Vitamin intakes were estimated from validated food frequency questionnaires in each study.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Among 501,857 women, 1,973 cases of ovarian cancer occurred over a median follow-up period of 7-16 years across studies.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The pooled multivariate RRs [95% confidence intervals (CIs)] for incremental increases in total intake of each vitamin were 1.02 (0.97-1.07) for vitamin A (increment: 1,300 mcg/day).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Dietary and total intakes of each vitamin were not significantly associated with ovarian cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.429.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We examined the associations between dietary and total (food and supplemental) vitamin intake and the risk of invasive epithelial ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Vitamin intakes were estimated from validated food frequency questionnaires in each study.

studies.Reference: Reproductive and dietary risk factors for epithelial ovarian cancer in China.
studies.Authors: Zhang M, Lee AH, Binns CW
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Information was collected using a structured questionnaire on sociodemographic and reproductive characteristics, diet, medical and family cancer history.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Cases were 254 patients with histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancer. Controls were 652 women without neoplasm.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The OR were 1.59 (95% CI 0.9-2.7) for retinol.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: No clear protective or harmful association was observed for retinol.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.098.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: The OR were 1.59 (95% CI 0.9-2.7) for retinol.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Cases were 254 patients with histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: The OR were 1.59 (95% CI 0.9-2.7) for retinol.

studies.Reference: Intakes of selected nutrients and food groups and risk of ovarian cancer.
studies.Authors: McCann SE, Moysich KB, Mettlin C
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Data on diet and other relevant risk factors in the few years before admission were collected with a self-administered questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 496 women with primary, histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancer and 1,425 women with nonneoplastic diagnoses.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Significantly reduced risks were associated with higher intakes of dietary fiber (OR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.38-0.87), vitamin A (OR = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.45-0.98).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Significantly reduced risks were associated with higher intakes of dietary fiber (OR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.38-0.87), vitamin A (OR = 0.66, 95% CI = 0.45-0.98).

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.5499). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 5 studies yielded an effect size of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.74–1.2), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin A and ovarian cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 65.07%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
